actions.text: Pressing Refresh re-fetches the list of log files.
Pressing Clear runs the DeleteLogFiles command and, when the command finishes, re-fetches the file list.
Choosing an entry in the nav menu navigates to the Log Files or Updater Log Files page.

rules.text: The same command is not sent again if it was run within the last 5 seconds; a warning is logged to the console instead.
The Clear button shows as executing only while the command status is queued or started.
This page is the application log view (type "app"), so it uses the "logs" folder.

shows.text: The page is titled "Log Files" with the heading scope "System".
A toolbar shows a logs navigation menu labelled with the current view, plus "Refresh" and "Clear" buttons.
The nav menu offers two entries: "Log Files" (/system/logs/files) and "Updater Log Files" (/system/logs/files/update).
An info box shows the log files location, built from the app data folder and the "logs" subfolder (or "UpdateLogs" for the updater view), joined with a backslash on Windows and a slash otherwise.
When the current view is "Log Files", the info box also shows a note about the default log level.
A loading indicator is shown while log files are being fetched.
When not fetching and files exist, a table lists the files, with one row per file.
Each row shows the filename, the last write time as a relative date, and a "Download" link that opens in a new tab.
When not fetching and there are no files, an info message for "no log files" is shown.
The Refresh icon spins while fetching, and the Clear icon spins while the delete-log-files command is queued or started.

sideEffects.text: Clear posts a new command to /command, and on success the command is added to the cached command list.
Loading the page requests the log file list from /log/file with the API key and client headers.
